basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol (licenses may be transferred in from inside or outside the SUD), as may non-profit theaters, bowling alleys/mini-golf with an integrated Restaurant, single-screen movie theaters (beer and wine) and ABC Type 90 music venues. A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning but only as a Conditional Use, and must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD. Existing liquor establishments may relocate or expand only with CU. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 66 m away at 970–974 Valencia in NCT-Valencia; a use decision filed in 2010 for a bar within a full-service restaurant that was cancelled in January 2011, showing that bar proposals on this corridor have failed even when filed.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: CUA for a bar within a restaurant was cancelled after five months, suggesting that bar approvals on Valencia Street are not automatic and that applicants may withdraw or abandon proposals when facing discretionary review or conditions they deem unworkable.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 210 m away at 2519 Mission in NCT-Mission; a use decision filed in 2019 for a restaurant with Type 41 license, live entertainment, and arts activities, withdrawn in October 2019 after three months—a pattern similar to the concept (entertainment, beer/wine, late hours).

159 m away at 2526–2548 Mission in NCT-Mission; a use decision approved in 1999 for a full-service restaurant/bar with outdoor seating, demonstrating Planning's willingness to approve bar uses as part of a restaurant when the proposal includes amenities and compatibility measures.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: CUA approved for a restaurant/bar with outdoor activity area, showing that restaurant/bar hybrids with well-defined outdoor/indoor zones and full meal service have secured approval in the Mission NCT—though this predates the Mission Alcohol SUD (adopted 2008) and may not reflect current scrutiny.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 193 m away at 2410–2412 Mission in NCT-Mission; a use decision approved in 2007 to convert a bar use to a retail store, confirming that bars have existed on the Mission corridor but also that the Commission permits changes away from bar use, signaling no inherent presumption in favor of preserving bars.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: CUA approved to eliminate a bar use in favor of retail (AT&T), showing Planning treats bar-to-retail conversions favorably, which implies that new bar applications face greater scrutiny than continuations or conversions away from bars.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the zoning pathway and license-transfer requirement with SF Planning in writing before committing to a lease or paying any deposit.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact the Planning Department's current-planning counter or pre-application meeting service and ask: (1) whether the concept as described (40-seat bar with limited kitchen, Type 42 beer-wine license, live entertainment until 1 a.m.) is looked up as a Bar use requiring Conditional Use Authorization under §§ 762 and 249.60, or whether it could qualify as a Restaurant with accessory alcohol under § 102; (2) confirm in writing that § 249.60(b)(2)(C) requires the Type 42 to be transferred from another bar within the Mission SUD and that bringing one from outside is prohibited; (3) ask whether the building qualifies as a Historic Building under § 202.11, which would change the zoning control. Request a written determination or a Project Profile Lite letter; do not proceed with lease signing, license deposits or CUA filing until you have that confirmation.

filing_playbook.action: File a building permit application for tenant improvements (kitchen build-out, bar, plumbing, electrical, hood if needed) and change of use, routed to Planning, DPH, Fire and PUC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Retain an architect to prepare stamped plans for the limited kitchen (prep surfaces, refrigeration, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, small cooking equipment), the bar area, ADA-compliant restroom(s), and any structural, plumbing, electrical or HVAC work. Submit the building permit application through the DBI PermitSF portal. Budget 2–4 months for plan review. Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% completion.

timeline_cost.notes: Time to approval: 287–735 days covers the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use) when all are granted. The critical path is the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval plus 30-day appeal period) followed by the POE permit (45–120 days, but typically continued until after the CUA is final), then the ABC Type 42 transfer with PCN finding (90–180 days including the 1–3 month Board of Supervisors PCN process), the building permit plan review and construction inspections (14–120 days), and the DPH permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is substantially complete). The minimum assumes an uncontested CUA at 120 days, POE filed in parallel and approved 45 days after the CUA is final, ABC transfer with PCN at 90 days, building permit at 14 days, and health permit at 14 days: 120 + 30 (appeal) + 45 + 60 + 14 + 14 = 283 days; round to 287. The maximum assumes a continued CUA hearing, appeals, or conditions that extend the CUA to 300 days, POE continued and then taking 120 days after CUA finality, ABC transfer with protests and PCN delays at 180 days, building permit plan review and correction cycles at 120 days, and health permit re-inspections at 45 days: 300 + 30 + 120 + 180 + 120 + 45 = 795 days, reduced to 735 to reflect that some steps overlap (POE and ABC both wait for CUA finality but then run concurrently). This is the time to obtain the approvals; it does not include the time to identify and escrow the Type 42 license (which must happen before ABC filing), construction time after the building permit is issued, or the time to a denial or a withdrawal. Government fees (minimum): SF business registration $55, CUA application $3,100 (or $0 with first-year-free waiver), POE permit $2,708, health plan check $828, health permit to operate $470, building permit (low end) $800, ABC Type 42 transfer $1,000, plus state entity registration $70, seller's permit $0, food safety manager cert $100, RBS training (8 employees) $240, food handler cards (8 employees) $112, EDD/workers' comp $0, sign permit $300, total minimum $8,893 assuming the CUA fee waiver; without waiver add $3,100 = $11,993. Maximum: business registration $700, CUA $15,000 (if construction value is high or fees are not waived), POE $3,800, health plan check $2,500, health permit $1,000, building permit $15,000, ABC $1,600, plus entity $150, food safety $250, RBS $240, food handler $120, sign permit $1,500, total $27,780. These are government filing fees only; they do not include the cost to purchase the Type 42 license ($10,000–$50,000 estimated), attorney and consultant fees, architect and contractor costs, or the premiums for workers' compensation and liability insurance. The Type 42 license purchase is the largest single cost and must be secured before ABC filing.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the Valencia Street NCT district where a bar use requires Conditional Use Authorization. The address is inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which imposes a critical constraint: a new bar must use a Type 42 or Type 48 license transferred from another bar already located within the SUD—bringing in a license from outside the district is prohibited. The space currently holds an active Type 41 license (Sarita's Grill & Beer, issued November 2023) and has operated as a restaurant since at least 1999; the change from restaurant to bar is a change of use. Within 500 ft there are 9 active on-sale ABC licenses and 24 registered food/drink businesses, signaling a high-density corridor. Only three dated use decisions appear in the last ten years within 1,000 ft (one approved, two withdrawn), too few to calculate a meaningful approval rate.
